#1706. Sergio Navarro’s style and the key individuals: Milan Futuro tactical analysis

Milan Futuro decided to go in a new direction this summer by appointing Sergio Navarro, but is it working so far?

Milan launched the Futuro project ahead of the 2024-25 season. with the aim of creating a pathway for academy players to break into the first team. The project was designed to bridge the physical and technical gap between the Primavera and senior football.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Things didn’t go well in year one, as Daniele Bonera didn’t see out the season as the head coach. He recently stated he didn’t think the squad was ready for the level, and ultimately Massimo Oddo was unable to save the team from relegation to Serie D, the fourth tier of Italian football.

With promotion back to Serie C the objective, this summer the Rossoneri turned to Sergio Navarro, a coach with good pedigree in Spain. The Futuro now appear to have a clearer structure, a defined playing identity and the right guidance, as Rohit Rajeev has outlined.

Under Barquero, Milan Futuro operate in a 4-2-3-1 formation. Asanji leads the line, with Ossola playing as the number 10 and Vos and Guernier occupying the wide positions.

Plazotta and Pandolfi form the double pivot, while Cisse and Pagliei partner at centre-back, with Perera and Colombo completing the back four.

Milan Futuro favour a possession-oriented approach, circulating the ball patiently at a measured tempo while waiting for gaps to emerge in the opposition’s defensive structure. They also use passing triangles effectively to create short passing options and play through the opposition’s high press.

In possession, Milan Futuro adopt a 3-1-6 structure, with Barquero showing little hesitation in committing players forward to create numerical overloads in the opposition half.

Asanji positions himself just behind the opposition’s defensive line, keeping the centre-backs occupied and preventing them from stepping forward freely. Meanwhile, Pandolfi and Plazotta maintain parallel positions in the double pivot, providing a stable base for the attacking structure.

In the opposition half, Milan Futuro keep the distances between players very short, allowing them to combine through quick, one-touch passes.

This also helps them create ball-sided overloads, with two or three players surrounding the Milan player in possession to provide close passing options. Once they enter the opposition half, the tempo increases as Milan look to become more direct and progress towards goal.

Similar to Amorim’s approach at Sporting, Milan Futuro form vertical corridors with three players positioned one behind another. This structure facilitates quick passing combinations while also creating movement to manipulate the opposition.

When Milan players drop to form these corridors or create overloads, they often drag defenders with them, opening spaces elsewhere to exploit.

Milan Futuro look to press the opposition high up the pitch, adopting a 4-4-2 shape with a man-oriented pressing scheme. This allows them to put pressure on the opposition’s build-up and restrict the time and space available to play out from the back.

Milan Futuro also set up pressing traps by deliberately leaving the opposition’s wide player unmarked. The pass towards the wide player acts as the pressing trigger, prompting Milan’s players to jump out of their positions and aggressively close down the receiver, while cutting off the available passing options.

Milan Futuro maintain an extremely narrow defensive shape, prioritising the protection of central spaces and forcing the opposition towards the flanks.

Once the opposition attempts to progress through the wide areas, the press shifts across to create numerical overloads around the ball, while Guernier and Colombo provide cover and prevent the opposition from switching play to the opposite flank.

Perhaps the most important aspect of Barquero’s approach is his willingness to build the system around his players’ strengths and allow them the freedom to express themselves.

Rather than focusing solely on tactical adaptability, he appears equally committed to their individual development and helping them grow as footballers. Here are a few examples.

One of Milan Futuro’s methods of chance creation is to play direct passes into Asanji. His ability to position himself between the ball and the opposition defender, using his physicality to shield possession and hold up play, is crucial to this approach.

Rather than asking him to adapt to the role of a more technically oriented, ball-playing striker, Barquero has built a mechanism that makes the most of his existing strengths.

Perhaps the clearest demonstration of Barquero’s coaching ability is his utilisation of Vos and Guernier. Guernier is a natural winger/forward, while Vos is more accustomed to playing as an attacking midfielder.

Within the 3-1-6 structure, Vos often inverts from the left flank into an inside-left role, allowing Perera to provide the width.

At times, he is also given the freedom to interchange positions with Plazotta, allowing him to drop into midfield or advance further up the pitch. This positional freedom helps him develop his midfield qualities and realise his potential.

Guernier, meanwhile, tends to maintain his width, stretching the opposition’s defensive line and creating space for Vos and the other attackers to exploit.

Barquero also gives Guernier the freedom to take on his direct opponent, even when he is outnumbered, allowing him to use his dribbling ability without being restricted by the team’s structure.

Ossola, who is particularly effective at receiving between the lines and turning with the ball, is allowed to operate higher up the pitch, closer to the opposition’s defensive line.

Idrissi, on the other hand, prefers to receive possession deeper, where he can dictate play with his passing range or carry the ball forward through dribbling.

#1705. Rayan to Liverpool or Manchester United? How the Brazilian’s style suits both clubs

By Alexis Pereira | 17 Nov 2026 18:16

Rayan is living a fast-moving career in European football. Signed by Bournemouth in January 2026 after standing out at Vasco da Gama, the Brazilian forward quickly won a place in the Premier League and began attracting the attention of bigger clubs. Liverpool are already monitoring his progress, while a statement has put Manchester United in the conversation: the player revealed that he has always supported the Red Devils because of Cristiano Ronaldo.

Andoni Iraola, who worked with Rayan at Bournemouth, took charge of Liverpool at the start of 2026-27. Manchester United have just appointed Mauricio Pochettino, a manager known for developing young attackers and for implementing a high-intensity style. But which of the two clubs would be the better destination for the Brazilian? The answer depends less on Rayan’s personal preference and more on the characteristics that have made him one of the most interesting prospects in Brazilian football.

Bournemouth paid Vasco €35m (about £30m) in January 2026, betting on a 19-year-old forward. Adaptation was quick: Rayan scored five goals and provided two assists in 15 games in the second half of last season.

His profile is different from a traditional winger who relies on short dribbles and quick changes of direction to beat a marker. Rayan is a player of strength and acceleration. When he receives with space, he can carry the ball at speed, protect possession with his body and attack the box with few touches.

In the 2025 Brazilian Serie A, Rayan was the player who finished the most carries with a shot, with 33 occasions. He also scored 14 goals in the league, a number that placed him among the competition’s top scorers. The forward is not just a winger who cuts inside, however. Under Fernando Diniz at Vasco, he was also used centrally, as a centre-forward, and showed an ability to win aerial balls and shield possession with his back to goal. His height and physical strength make it possible to imagine growth in that role, although he still has to improve his control and combination play under pressure.

It is also important to consider what is left to develop. Rayan can still improve the quality of his final pass, his choice of moments to shoot and his involvement in building play. Despite the volume of carries that ended in shots, his creative output was more limited. That helps explain why he still needs an environment that gives him freedom to attack without requiring him to be the main organiser of the attack.

This season, the Brazilian has played ten Premier League games, with one goal and no assists. The output does not match his arrival in England, but Rayan remains a frequent starter and is still adapting to a new manager and a model different from Iraola’s.

Liverpool’s interest strengthened after Iraola’s arrival. The Reds followed the Brazilian closely early in the season and could consider a move in 2027. Iraola knows Rayan’s virtues and limitations. It was under his management that the Brazilian began adapting to the intensity of the Premier League, playing mainly on the right and being given freedom to attack space.

The manager also played a part in the step up of other Bournemouth players, such as Antoine Semenyo, who stood out before moving to Manchester City. Tactically, the combination makes sense. Iraola’s teams usually press high, try to win the ball back in advanced areas and accelerate as soon as they find space. He does not demand that his wingers stay tied to the touchline: they can attack inside, combine with the full-backs and appear in different channels. Rayan could play on the right, cutting inside onto his left foot, but also attack depth and offer a physical threat in transitions.

At Liverpool, that characteristic could be useful. The team has changed in attack: Bradley Barcola, Cody Gakpo, Victor Munoz and Rio Ngumoha offer alternatives, but Rayan would add a different profile, a more powerful forward able to carry the ball at speed and attack the box.

There is one caveat. Liverpool already have quality attacking options. The manager also has to manage a more demanding calendar and a team with title ambitions. Rayan could find a way to play, but would hardly have the same freedom as a young player developing at Bournemouth.

Rayan’s link with Manchester United came to light in an interview with ESPN. The forward said he has always supported the club in England because of Cristiano Ronaldo, his great idol. He also recalled the emotion of playing at Old Trafford and beating the Red Devils 3-0 with Bournemouth in October.

The statement became relevant when United hired Pochettino to try to reorganise a team going through a difficult season. The Argentinian has a track record of developing young players and built his best work in England with intense teams, aggressive in the press and quick in transitions. His most usual model starts from a 4-2-3-1, with wingers who often attack inside spaces and full-backs who push on to give width.

That structure could favour Rayan. Starting from the right, the Brazilian would have freedom to carry towards the box, finish with his left foot and attack the spaces created by team-mates’ movement. High pressing also suits his physical ability, although defensive involvement is still an area he needs to improve.

The problem is competition. United already have Bryan Mbeumo, Amad Diallo and Matheus Cunha among their attacking options, plus Benjamin Sesko as a central reference. There is also a developmental question. Pochettino usually demands a lot from his players without the ball and works with coordinated attacking movements. For a forward who still needs to improve decision-making and creation, the environment can be positive but also brings high demands. The Brazilian would need to learn to alternate individual carrying with quick combination play and movement without the ball.

United, on the other hand, could offer room to grow if Pochettino sees Rayan as a medium-term project and not an immediate solution to attacking problems. The Argentinian’s ability to develop young forwards is a point in favour, but the squad already has players in similar roles.

Between the two scenarios, Liverpool appear to offer the clearer fit. Iraola already knows the Brazilian, knows how to use his strength in transitions and has a model that favours attackers able to carry the ball at speed. The departure of Mohamed Salah has also opened space for a reorganisation of the right side, making the position a concrete possibility for Rayan.

Manchester United have the emotional appeal and a manager whose philosophy could match the Brazilian’s characteristics. But the presence of Mbeumo, Amad and Cunha makes the battle for space more complex. To turn admiration for the club into a transfer, Rayan would need to see a clear sporting plan.

At any rate, the moment is still one of development. At 20, the forward does not need to choose immediately between two giants, especially as he has a contract with Bournemouth until 2031 and is still gaining experience in a demanding league. Rayan has the attributes to reach a top-level club, but his next step needs to be defined by the project that best uses his potential. Between his familiarity with Iraola and his identification with United, Liverpool appear to have a tactical advantage.

#1704. Vitoria vs Bragantino - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 17 Nov 2026 18:17

Vitoria will be looking to end a five-match winless run when they welcome Bragantino to the Estadio Manoel Barradas on Thursday in a Campeonato Brasileiro Serie A encounter.

The hosts sit 15th in the table with 38 points from 34 matches, just one point above the relegation zone, while Braga occupy eighth place with 47 points and are hoping to keep their hopes of qualifying for the 2027 Copa Libertadores alive.

Vitoria head into Thursday's encounter under pressure after losing 3-0 at home to Fluminense in their most recent league outing, a result that extended their winless run to five matches.

The Rubro-Negro had previously suffered a 2-0 defeat away to Coritiba, following consecutive 1-1 draws against Athletico Paranaense and Corinthians, while their earlier meeting with Sao Paulo ended in a 2-1 loss.

Their last league victory came on October 8, when they thrashed Chapecoense 4-0 at home, leaving them with only two points from the last five matches, the fewest points by any team in the league in that period.

The defeat to Fluminense also marked a difficult end to Jair Ventura's time in charge, with the coach dismissed after Vitoria slipped to within one point of the relegation zone.

Rafael Lacerda has been appointed and will take charge of his first match on Thursday, having had the international break to work with the squad and prepare for the challenge ahead.

Vitoria's home record offers some encouragement, however, as they have won 10 of their 17 league matches at the Barradao, drawing twice and losing five times, though they are without a win in their last two games as hosts.

Bragantino, meanwhile, arrive in Salvador after recording consecutive victories, having beaten Chapecoense 3-0 before securing a 2-1 home win over Santos in their most recent match.

Massa Bruta took the lead against Santos via an own goal from Rodinei, before conceding an equaliser in the 37th minute, but Wallace Yan scored his third goal in two games to claim all three points.

Vagner Mancini's side have now won three of their last five league matches, drawing once and losing once, with their other victory coming in a 4-2 home success over Cruzeiro, while they recorded a 1-1 draw away to Remo during that period, with their only defeat coming against Palmeiras, who beat them 2-0 in Sao Paulo.

Braga’s away form has been less convincing than their home performances, having won only four of their 17 matches on the road, drawing five and losing eight, while they are without a win in their last eight league games and last 10 across all competitions.

However, the head-to-head record also gives the visitors reason for optimism, having won the last two meetings between the clubs, though the Massa Bruta have lost the last two on the road.

Vitoria will be without several players through injury, including Nathan Mendes, Fabiano Souza, Edu, Camutanga, Ramon and Riccieli, while Dudu is also listed as unavailable.

Luan Candido and Nacho Laquintana are expected to miss out because they are on loan from Bragantino and their agreements reportedly include clauses requiring Vitoria to pay a fee for each player to feature against their parent club.

Emmanuel Britez is available again after serving a suspension, and the defender is expected to partner Caca in central defence.

Lacerda is also likely to retain Lucas Arcanjo in goal, with Rene, Erick and Matheuzinho among the attacking options as he prepares for his first match in charge.

Bragantino will be without Lucas Barbosa, who is suspended, while Rodriguinho and Davi Gomes are sidelined through injury.

Jose Hurtado is also a doubt after picking up a thigh injury, leaving Mancini with some decisions to make in defence as he attempts to maintain his team's recent momentum.

Yan is expected to retain his place in the attacking midfield, while Eduardo Sasha should lead the line.

However, Bragantino's recent improvement should allow them to compete, and we expect both sides to find the net before sharing the points.

#1703. GdS: Worth the price tag – how Moreira became ‘untouchable’ for Milan and Belgium

It has been a positive international break for Diego Moreira, who continued his excellent form from club football.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write this morning, Ruben Amorim will welcome Moreira back to Milanello soon. The winger has become a regular starter and producing goals and assists, but the Portuguese coach knows the pitfalls of the match against Frosinone all too well.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Therefore, starting Thursday – when the squad will be fully back together after the day off tomorrow – everyone’s minds will be focused solely on the new busy schedule awaiting the Rossoneri until Christmas. More specifically, seven matches from Sunday until December 19th.

Immediately after the last international break, the Rossoneri drew away to Sassuolo, a result that certainly wasn’t greeted with a smile. The goal is to avoid repeating that misstep against Alvini’s team, and Moreira will be key to that.

Despite his 22 years of age and the €50m valuation plus bonuses that could have weighed heavily on his shoulders, Diego hasn’t taken long to win over Milan fans. In his last six league matches (he missed two due to injury), he’s scored four goals and provided three assists.

He has also demonstrated his ability to switch roles with ease, playing as a winger on the right or left, as a wing-back or even as a full-back. He plays with the boldness of someone who targets his opponent and tries to dribble past him, something that fans always appreciate.

Moreira always seeks one-on-one situations, both due to his strengths and the explicit request of Amorim, who asks his wide players to create numerical superiority. Diego is succeeding remarkably, as his assist for Christian Pulisic in the derby shows, as he got past Carlo Augusto and crossed.

Moreira made the difference against Italy on Sunday too: not only did he score the fourth goal, which he celebrated by making a gesture of ‘one, two, three and four’ with his fingers, but he also kept accelerating, hit the woodwork, shot wide once more and had two shots blocked by his opponents.

He set up De Bruyne for a shot, had more touches than anyone else in the opponents’ area (11) and often took on Calafiori and Dimarco, delighting the crowd with a spectacular backheel. He had around 50 touches and 27/31 completed passes, earning the applause of the entire stadium when he came off.

Moreira is currently captivating thanks to his drive and desire. He’s that way at Milan and he’s that way with the national team. That’s why there’s a version of the Rossoneri with him and another without him which, frankly, isn’t as threatening.

Amorim carefully integrated him into the team’s operations at the start of the season, but now he has broken the padlock off and now considers him a key player in the team. This doesn’t mean he won’t need a breather, given the schedule, but the coach will have to think about the right moments to rest.

With four goals in Serie A (one every 121 minutes), he’s already matched his four goals from last season in Ligue 1, and he has no intention of stopping. He feels the confidence in himself and the team.

The leap from Ligue 1 to Serie A didn’t bother him. In fact, he intends to continue dancing on the pitch, just like in the derby or against Italy. On Sunday, he wants to show he has the same energy with which he brought Italy to its knees. Milan and San Siro await him.

#1702. Report: €70m Liverpool deal hinges on one major decision

Liverpool have already been linked with a lot of players ahead of the January transfer window.

The Anfield outfit are fourth in the Premier League which, after all the money they've spent, is a massive underperformance.

One of the best ways for the Reds to combat this is to sign new players to plug the gaps their current squad are leaving open.

Obviously, some positions are more of a problem than others with Liverpool likely to have a priority position that they want to strengthen.

But, if they manage to cover all the potential positions they need to, they'll have a massive selection of players to choose from which would obviously be beneficial for them.

Since the Reds aren't a club who have an endless amount of money to spend, their transfers need to mean something which is why their next big deal is hinging on a major decision from the Anfield outfit.

Liverpool are unlikely to sign Lamine Camara in January

Lamine Camara was one of the main players linked with a Liverpool transfer in the summer.

It was clear to almost everyone that a new midfielder was one of the main things that Iraola needed to take the Reds to the next level.

Obviously, replacing Mohamed Salah was also one of the main things that they needed to do but, with how much players such as Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch have struggled to adapt to Iraola's system, the Reds have managed to dig themselves into a bit of a hole.

Because, even though they were desperate for a new midfielder in the summer, by January, it'll be more than clear to every team in the world that a new midfielder is required by the Reds.

In the summer, Camara was available for a cut-rate deal and now, he's worth around €70 million.

The fact of Szoboszlai and Gravenberch also having prominent roles among their ranks also needs to be taken into consideration as, if another midfielder is brought in, the minutes played by each player will diminish.

And, according to David Lynch via Anfield Index, this could be the thing to stop them from signing the Senegal international.

"I know the reports, but still struggle to see Lamine Camara to Liverpool in January without a significant departure," he said.

"Endo doesn’t play at all, more a Gravenberch or Szoboszlai which it’s hard to see, otherwise there’s a question of minutes. Liverpool don’t like to be over stocked as we know."

Lamine Camara would be a perfect transfer for Liverpool

Before the summer, Camara was probably a player that most Liverpool fans won't have heard of.

The midfielder was quietly making a name for himself in Ligue 1 and then, when Filipe Luis took over as their manager, he instantly became one of the first names on their team sheet.

From that point on, clubs from across the world were interested in the midfielder and have remained so ever since.

But, of all the teams he's been linked with, Liverpool are the team he'd be perfect for.

Not only would he perfectly fit into Iraola's plans but, he'd also be able to come in for one of his starting midfielders.

Indeed, the €70 million fee is a bit of a risk but, in reality, that's the going rate for a decent central midfielder these days.

Here's hoping that Liverpool come to their senses and get a deal over the line.

#1701. Declan Rice’s new five-year deal to 2031 marks his rise from £105m signing to Arsenal leader

By Alexis Pereira | 17 Nov 2026 18:28

Declan Rice’s new contract with Arsenal recognises a transformation built over three seasons. When he arrived at the Emirates Stadium in July 2023, the midfielder was a high-impact signing: he cost £105m, a record for a British player at the time, and carried the expectation of lifting a team that had just lost the Premier League title to Manchester City.

Today, at 27, Rice is an English champion, one of the leaders of the dressing room and one of the team’s technical reference points. The new five-year deal shows Arsenal’s intention to keep him at the centre of the project through his physical and technical peak. It also reflects his changing status within the club, as Rice is expected to earn a salary close to that of Bukayo Saka, until now the squad’s top earner.

Rice was not just an expensive signing who lived up to expectations. He became a more complete player, widened his influence across different phases of play and took on responsibilities beyond his role in midfield. The promise of 2023 has become one of the faces of a championship team and a leader for the cycle that starts now.

Rice’s arrival came at a decisive moment for Mikel Arteta’s project. In 2022-23, Arsenal spent much of the season at the top but lost steam in the closing stretch and finished five points behind Manchester City. The team had shown that they could compete for the title, but they needed more quality, depth and experience to sustain a challenge to the end.

Rice had characteristics that answered several of those needs. At 24, he was already West Ham United’s captain, had experience with England and had just won the Conference League. Arsenal beat the competition and completed the signing for £100m fixed plus £5m in bonuses.

The fee raised expectations. It was not enough for Rice to be a good holding midfielder: he had to justify a historic investment and help Arsenal take the step needed to compete with City. His first season showed the scale of the signing quickly.

Rice played 38 Premier League games, scoring seven goals and providing eight assists. The number of goal contributions was a considerable improvement on his West Ham record, but his impact was not limited to attacking output. Arsenal again finished as runners-up, but Rice had already become one of the team’s most important players. The signing did not deliver an immediate title, but it helped turn expectation into a conviction that the club had found a midfielder able to carry their project for many years.

Rice’s development also reflects the way Arteta changed his use. Early in his time at Arsenal, the Englishman often played as the deepest midfielder, responsible for protecting the defence and offering a reference point for build-up. It was a familiar role, close to the one he had at West Ham, but it did not use his full repertoire.

After an adaptation period, especially from the start of 2024, Arteta began using him more often as a box-to-box midfielder on the left. The change let Rice use one of his main qualities: carrying the ball at speed, breaking lines and arriving in the opposition area while still contributing to defensive recovery.

The Englishman gained more freedom to attack space, appear at the edge of the box and join attacking combinations. His physical power became a weapon for taking Arsenal into the opposition half, while his ability to get back helped keep balance when the team lost the ball. Instead of just protecting team-mates, Rice also began to drive the team.

Set pieces were another important tool. Rice began taking corners and free-kicks, using the accuracy of his delivery and his ability to put the ball in dangerous areas. Since his arrival, he has provided ten assists from set pieces in the Premier League. His two free-kick goals against Real Madrid in the 2024-25 Champions League quarter-finals were the most emblematic moment of that evolution.

Versatility does not mean Rice has no fixed position or needs to take part in every attacking action. The most recent development lies in choosing moments. With Martin Zubimendi, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Martin Odegaard offering different partnership options, Arteta has alternated the height at which the Englishman receives the ball and the freedom he has to advance.

The ability to perform different roles is one of the reasons Rice has become so important to Arteta. In the title-winning season, he was used both as the most advanced midfielder and in a midfield pair alongside Zubimendi. He is not just a player who adapts to different positions: he lets the manager change the structure of the team without necessarily changing personnel.

Rice’s growth was not only tactical. Over the seasons, he also became one of the squad’s main voices. His direct personality, willingness to demand more from team-mates and ability to take responsibility in difficult moments made him a reference point for the group.

One example came in April, when Odegaard was out injured and Rice was given the captain’s armband. He had worn it on other occasions, but the choice reinforced a perception that had been building: his influence does not depend on being the official captain.

In Arsenal’s 2025-26 Premier League title, which ended a 22-year wait for the competition, Rice was one of the protagonists of the campaign, with 36 appearances, four goals and five assists in the league. More than his statistical contribution, his ability to maintain intensity in different roles was fundamental.

Declan Rice at Arsenal - all competitions since joining in July 2023 2023-24: 51 games, 48 starts, 33 wins, 8 draws, 10 defeats, 7 goals, 9 assists (64.7% wins) 2024-25: 52 games, 48 starts, 28 wins, 16 draws, 8 defeats, 9 goals, 10 assists (53.8% wins) 2025-26: 55 games, 49 starts, 37 wins, 12 draws, 6 defeats, 5 goals, 9 assists (67.3% wins) 2026-27 (in progress): 15 games, 14 starts, 13 wins, 1 draw, 1 defeat, 1 goal, 5 assists (86.7% wins) Total: 173 games, 159 starts, 111 wins, 37 draws, 25 defeats, 22 goals, 33 assists (64.2% wins)

Trophies for Arsenal (3): Premier League 2025-26, Community Shield 2023, Community Shield 2026

Official matches only (Premier League, Champions League, FA Cup, EFL Cup and Community Shield). Matches decided on penalties count as draws. Data up to 16 November 2026. Sources: FBref (Opta data), BeSoccer and Opta Analyst.

The challenge now is to sustain this level without ignoring fatigue. Rice has come from seasons with a high volume of games, often exceeding 50 matches for club and country. Last season, he played 54 games for Arsenal in all competitions, in addition to England commitments. Managing his workload will be important for him to keep his influence over a demanding calendar.

By extending his contract to 2031, Arsenal secure a player who still has years at his peak ahead and who already knows Arteta’s demands in depth. The club no longer need to wait for Rice to become a leader: that stage has already happened. Now the expectation is that he helps lead the next chapters of a project that intends to keep competing for the main trophies.

#1700. Report: Barcelona set price and now Liverpool deal can move forward

Liverpool can move forward with a transfer after Barcelona named their price for the player. The ball is firmly in the Reds' court now.

Liverpool need a new left-back. That much is abundantly clear to everyone and it’s something that will inevitably happen in 2027 - it’s just a matter of when.

They might move in January, depending on how Andoni Iraola views the current squad. It’s clear he’s not enamoured with either Milos Kerkez or Kostas Tsimikas by the way he’s constantly rotating the pair.

Kerkez, though, is here for the long term. Liverpool invested in him and he’s still so young - there’s zero reason to write him off at this stage and we’re still confident that he’ll make it at Anfield.

However, Tsimikas’s contract expires next summer and we see no real chance that he gets a new one. Liverpool will have to find competition for Kerkez, both to give him a reason to keep pushing and to hedge the bets here.

Liverpool, after all, are far more likely to find an elite left-back if they’re investing in two, rather than going all-in on Kerkez.

Barcelona set Alex Balde priceBarcelona have reportedly set their price for Alejandro Balde. The full-back is wanted by several clubs across Europe, including Juventus. Corriere dello Sport reports on the back of that. They're saying that Barcelona are open to a loan deal, which may suit Juve, but would also sell permanently at €40m and above.

Barcelona have reportedly set their price for Alejandro Balde. The full-back is wanted by several clubs across Europe, including Juventus.

Corriere dello Sport reports on the back of that. They're saying that Barcelona are open to a loan deal, which may suit Juve, but would also sell permanently at €40m and above.

Liverpool are also interested in Balde. The player wasn't keen on leaving Catalonia back in the summer but things have reportedly changed. His agent, Jorge Mendes, has held tentative talks with the Reds, supposedly.

The door is now open, then. A deal with the Reds has room to move forward with Barcelona's price now known and the real question is whether Liverpool actually want to pay that.

It's essentially what they paid for Kerkez and the idea of having two left-backs worth over €40m does seem a bit mad. Especially when so many other areas of the squad require consideration and probably investment.

Balde, though, may be as sure of a thing as Liverpool can get at that price point. One thing's for sure - it'll tempt them.

#1699. Flamengo vs Athletico Paranaense - prediction, team news, lineups

By Saikat Mandal | 17 Nov 2026 19:11

With four rounds remaining in the Brasileirao, Flamengo host Athletico Paranaense on Wednesday night, November 18, as their title defence enters its decisive stage.

Having collected 92% of the available points in the second half of the season, Flamengo can take a significant step towards back-to-back titles and put themselves in a stronger position ahead of their huge clash against Palmeiras in the following round. Athletico Paranaense, meanwhile, face an uphill task to break back into the top four, having gone four matches without a win and with the tournament's leading scorer unavailable.

In the fight for back-to-back titles and a ninth Brasileirao crown, Flamengo return from this FIFA international break with good news: their key players delivered excellent performances and, more importantly, came back from international duty without any injuries.

Giorgian de Arrascaeta once again took centre stage for the Rubro-Negro with the Uruguay national team. Having had a direct hand in both of Uruguay’s goals against Argentina at the Bombonera, Flamengo’s number 10 also became the first foreigner to have a bust unveiled at the club’s headquarters, in a ceremony on Sunday, November 15.

Bruno Henrique also received the honour and looked ahead to the business end of the season: “We know there is not much left before the year ends, there are four games, so we will give everything in these games to win the title. God willing, we can celebrate in December as well,” he said at the event.

Right-back Guillermo Varela, meanwhile, produced a solid display, playing the full 95 minutes of the match in Buenos Aires. Although Argentina’s goal came down his side, he was not at fault.

Nicolas de la Cruz and Ecuadorians Gonzalo Plata and Anthony Valencia did not leave the bench, but the latter two still have a friendly against Bolivia on Tuesday night, November 17.

Athletico Paranaense, for their part, are enjoying a notable campaign for a newly promoted side. However, in the fight for a direct spot in next season’s Libertadores, the Furacao suffered a heavy blow at Brazil’s sports court (STJD).

In a hearing on Monday, November 16, Kevin Viveros had his ban extended to three matches. The Brasileirão’s top scorer with 21 goals was sent off in the 3-1 defeat to Vasco on November 4, for a stamp on full-back Cuiabano.

As a result, he will not return until the final round, against Sao Paulo at the Arena da Baixada. Jorge Rivaldo and Renan Peixoto are the natural options given their profile, but manager Odair Hellmann could also opt to use forward Kerwin Vargas in an adapted role.

In the same hearing, the Parana side were also punished. The fine for racist gestures attributed to a fan during the match against Vasco was increased to R$30,000 (approximately £4,200). The decision was taken by a majority of votes.

Currently fifth with 54 points, Athletico could close the gap on Fluminense, who occupy the final Libertadores spot. Bahia and Atletico Mineiro, however, are also in the same points range.

In a late development, Gonzalo Plata was released from the Ecuador squad for “personal reasons” and could become an unexpected boost. Having played just 13 minutes against Costa Rica, he should not, in theory, show any physical wear.

Nicolas de la Cruz and Anthony Valencia remain with their national teams and are not expected to return in time.

On the medical front, experienced left-back Alex Sandro has recovered from muscular oedema in his left thigh and has returned to training with the group, although Ayrton Lucas is expected to be the first choice for Portuguese manager Leonardo Jardim.

Midfielder Lucas Paqueta has not yet fully recovered from a knee problem sustained during the thrashing of Vasco, so he is unlikely to be included without a reasonable amount of training, according to Jardim himself. Danilo, meanwhile, continues his recovery schedule following a jaw fracture and also remains sidelined.

The point of concern is the number of players one booking away from suspension: Leo Pereira, Alex Sandro, Erick Pulgar, Arrascaeta, Pedro, Bruno Henrique, Luiz Araujo and Vitao. Should any of them be booked by referee Rafael Klein, they would miss the clash against Palmeiras in the following round.

Besides Viveros, Dantas is also serving a suspension due to the automatic one-match ban for a third yellow card. Young centre-back Arthur Dias, who is attracting interest from several European clubs, is another absentee. He is set to play for the Brazil national team against Singapore and is not expected to return to Brazil in time.

Defender Lucas Esquivel is still recovering from a hip injury and will be assessed on matchday, but he is expected to complete the back line alongside Gaston Benavidez and Juan Aguirre. Goalkeeper Santos and Bruno Zapelli could be given a chance in the starting eleven.

Agustin Rossi; Varela, Leo Pereira, Leo Ortiz, Ayrton Lucas; Pulgar, Jorginho, Arrascaeta; Carrascal, Pedro, Samuel Lino. Manager: Leonardo Jardim.

Athletico Paranaense possible starting lineup:

Santos; Benavidez, Aguirre, Esquivel; Gilberto, Luiz Gustavo, Jadson, Mendoza; Bruno Zapelli, Joao Cruz, Kerwin Vargas. Manager: Odair Hellmann.

Athletico's task would have been difficult enough as it is, but with their top scorer and best defender both unavailable, it is hard to see the visitors taking anything from this encounter.

For Flamengo, the priority will be to maintain their formidable home record and head into the most eagerly anticipated game of the year in a favourable position. A convincing victory at the Maracana would be the ideal way to achieve that.

#1698. Di Marzio: Endrick and Tresoldi deals ‘not a financial issue’ for Milan – the situation

AC Milan have the financial capability to go out and sign their top targets in January, according to Gianluca Di Marzio.

Several reports and even the words of owner Gerry Cardinale have made it very clear that Milan plan to be busy in the winter mercato. The main target seems to be a forward to complete the attack, as well as a centre-back to help out the defensive department too.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Among the names linked have been Real Madrid’s Endrick, Club Brugge’s Nicolo Tresoldi and Sporting CP’s Goncalo Inacio. It’s one thing having the list of names, but it is another having the money and the possibility of doing a deal mid-season with the selling club.

During last night’s segment on Sky, Gianluca Di Marzio (via MilanNews) was asked whether Milan can realistically pursue names like Endrick and Tresoldi, who are likely to cost over €50m each.

“That they has the strength to do these kinds of deals, yes. They demonstrated it over the summer, so I don’t think there’s a financial issue,” he began.

“Whether they manage to sign one of the two… Endrick, as far as we know, José Mourinho hasn’t changed his mind and therefore doesn’t intend to part with him in January. But Endrick is a Cardinale obsession, just as he was a Roma obsession during the summer.

“We’ll have to see if Mourinho changes his mind in the month and a half before the transfer window opens. He hasn’t changed his mind at the moment, so I see the situation as complicated at the moment.

“Just as it’s complicated for Brugge to sell Tresoldi. Brugge are a club that doesn’t need to sell and always sells at least one key player in the summer, precisely to try to get to the end of the season with its players.

“Milan are looking for a striker, looking for a back-up for Ramos. The figures I’ve read, 60-70 million, are very, very high figures to try to convince Brugge to sell him. It’s a deal that – given the player’s objective value – I think is around 50 million. In my opinion.

“But Brugge are unlikely to sell him in January. Above all, Milan is looking for a striker to be a back-up for Ramos; it’s not like Ramos and Tresoldi will play together. In the sense that Milan has always played with a centre-forward.

“Above all, they need to provide this center forward with plenty of playable balls rather than buy another. Because if Ramos doesn’t receive balls in the penalty area, he struggles to score, and Tresoldi struggles to score either.

“They need a striker to get Camarda playing. I think Camarda will go and play and therefore an investment will be needed in a player who can be a suitable deputy for Ramos.”

#1697. Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat

Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.

Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.

There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.

Juventus were the victors though, thanks to a sumptuous 68th-minute goal by Kosovo winger Edon Zhegrova.

Alonso had 21 players on his bench, and made 12 second-half substitutions.

Levi Colwill and Cole Palmer featured in the defeat by 10-man Spurs on Saturday, but sat this game out as they continue to build fitness. Danny Welbeck did start though, reunited with former Brighton team-mate Joao Pedro up top.

Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

Chelsea continue their pre-season against AC Milan on Saturday, before they host Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on August 15.

They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

Even Chelsea’s in-house streaming had given up the ghost by the end. Consecutive pre-season defeats for Chelsea, but worth remembering that Colwill and Palmer sat out this fitness exercise and Enzo Fernandez is still to return. Palestra’s performances a real positive but the team is still finding its way.

Juventus win a corner late on, but Yildiz’s delivery is too close to Penders. Just two minutes for Chelsea to find an equaliser.

Mudryk does well to dig out a cross from the left but the goalkeeper Perin gathers. There will be four minutes of added time to play.

Chelsea not really threatening an equaliser as the game meanders towards a conclusion. Should they score a goal, we will have a penalty shoot-out.

Estevao looked for Mudryk with a reverse pass between full-back and centre-back but there was too much weight on the ball.

Estevao’s free-kick is saved but the bigger news for Chelsea fans is that Mykhailo Mudryk has been introduced from the bench, replacing Nicolas Jackson for the closing stages.

Lavia and Liam Delap involved in some handbags with the Juventus players, Bremer the centre-back in the thick of things too and has been shown a yellow card. Chelsea have a free-kick, Estevao over it from 35 yards out.

Just the one goal scored for Chelsea against top level opponents in pre-season, but I doubt Alonso will be panicking just yet. Chelsea play Milan this weekend before hosting Real Sociedad on August 15th in their final pre season friendly.

Juventus goalkeeper Perin sells Nicolas Jackson a dummy so he can pick a pass into midfield. The Italian side controlling the game quite well since the goal, against a weaker Chelsea team.

Chelsea’s younger players will have to dig them out of trouble in the last 20 minutes. There has not been much in the game, Chelsea have shaded it in general play without quite creating enough.

The Kosovan winger with a first-time, left-footed hit from almost 25 yards, curled into the top corner. Nothing Penders could do about it.

More changes from Chelsea: Anselmino, Acheampong, Satpaev, Assugo and Delap the players on, replacing Hato, Palestra, Gittens, Caicedo and Pedro. Alonso finishing the team with his younger players on the pitch.

Jonathan David slides a pass across the Chelsea six-yard box when there was a chance to shoot, but the flag was up for offside in any case.

Penders does well to palm away an inswinging cross from Zhegrova, before Estevao picks out the run of Palestra on the break with a brilliant forward pass. Chelsea corner, cleared. Now Caicedo has been booked for a cynical challenge to stop a break, much like Douglas Luiz.

Nicolas Jackson hacked down by Douglas Luiz after he turned on halfway with three or four Chelsea runners in support. Painful one for Jackson, and a yellow card for the former Aston Villa midfielder. Chelsea players not happy with that challenge in a pre-season game.

Chelsea certainly have the upper hand in the game, quick feet from Joao Pedro to win a free-kick in midfield. If either team is going to score the game’s first goal, you fancy it will be them.

This time Chelsea find Palestra with a ball over the top, but his shot at goal is at a comfortable height for the goalkeeper.

Palestra popping up in a centre-forward position again, but his shot towards goal is not struck cleanly. The right-back at the heart of Chelsea’s attacking again.

Two very different XIs out there for the second half.

Penders replaces Sanchez in goal, Sarr on for Tosin, Estevao on for Quenda and Jackson on for Welbeck.

For Juventus: Bremer, Perin, Zhegrova, Owusu and David are on.

Not much to write/phone/WhatsApp home about, so far. The combination between Quenda and Palestra down Chelsea’s right has been the best feature of their football, am sure we will see Estevao on that flank in the second half among other changes. The bumpy pitch and a hydration break has not helped the spectacle.

There will be four minutes of stoppage time, simply a result of the hydration break.

Far too much space opens up between Chelsea’s defence and midfield, with Meritti turning and carrying the ball forward. Boga tests Sanchez with a strike from the edge of the box. That was probably Juventus’s most threatening attack.

Palestra defends well as the last man up against Milik, Chelsea almost undone by Locatelli’s outside of the foot pass.

Robert Sanchez caught under a cross swung to the back post, very unconvincing goalkeeping, but Juventus could not get their shot away in the box. Nicoll-Jazuli then did well to bring the ball away for Chelsea at the edge of the box.

Chelsea have another corner, and yet again it comes from a right-sided attack. Chelsea are in ascendancy now after a slow start, but it is a very low intensity contest.

Caicedo with a couple of threatening crosses from a centre-right position, but no Chelsea player can connect with them cleanly. Gittens’s dribbling down the left causing problems for Cambiaso, and he was the one attacking Caicedo’s cross at the back post.

Play has now resumed after the drinks break. No changes from either team, those will come at half time. Chelsea have 21 players sitting on their bench, albeit a number of academy players are on tour.

Time for a hydration break, even though the game is being played under a closed roof.

Chelsea’s right side is their most dangerous, by a distance. Quenda does well to slip Palestra in on the overlap, and his low cross into the six-yard box is cleared for a corner. Juventus clear. Boga with a burst through the Chelsea midfield but the Juventus man then gets his pass wrong.

Kelly with a left-to-right switch to Cambiaso, and his cross deflects off the toe of Miretti in the middle and trickles just wide of the far post. Sanchez was scrambling but I think the goalkeeper had it covered.

Chelsea enjoying their most sustained spell of possession in Juventus’s half so far, without quite carving out a clear cut chance. Juventus defending their penalty area with a back five, but they do not have Bonucci, Chiellini and Barzagli back there anymore.

Quenda with a threatening inswinging cross from the right flank, but Welbeck could not quite rise high enough to direct his header towards the far corner. Quenda was keeping the width for Chelsea with Palestra inside the winger in the box. Quenda then slices a shot over from long range.

Welbeck and Caicedo involved in some good combination play, with Nicoll-Jazuli’s outside of the foot pass finding Gittens. Chelsea’s left-winger runs into traffic, but he has been one of the bright spots of the pre-season campaign thus far.

Having watched a couple of Chelsea’s friendlies, there is a lot to like about Palestra at right-back. Tall, long stride, lots of composure on the ball. Will be interesting to see if they can find a way for him and Reece James to start games. Chelsea as a team yet to find much rhythm in the game so far.

Tosin could well find himself down the pecking order this season among Chelsea’s raft of centre-backs, but he makes an important block in the area before Locatelli drags a shot wide from the edge of the box.

Former Bournemouth defender Lloyd Kelly is in the Juventus team. The Italian team are looking to press high in the early minutes whenever Chelsea try to play out from the back. Quenda with an early dart at the Juventus defence but he gets the pass all wrong with Palestra overlapping.

Palestra with a loose first touch but he recovers and defends well. Like in Sydney, this looks another very bumpy pitch, you can see the join marks between the pieces of turf that have been freshly laid. Coming out of these games without any injuries will be a priority for Alonso.

Juventus get the game started in their pale pink away kit.

Juventus XI: Di Gregorio, Kalulu, Gatti, Kelly, Cambiaso, Douglas Luiz, Locatelli, Miretti, Boga, Milik, Celik

Subs: Perrin, Pinsoglio, Nava, Bremmer, Rugani, Koopmeiners, Arthur Melo, Cabal, Owusu, Gil Puche, Oboavwoduo, Licina, Durmisi, Yildiz, Zhegrova, David

Welbeck starts against Juventus, but no Jordan Henderson with the group just yet. As Sam Dean writes here: “Last season, especially, provided evidence that the balance of their squad was not right, and they are now trying to change the internal dynamic by adding more leadership and experience to the team.”

How long will he stay there? Will he play his way back into Alonso’s team, be shipped out on loan or sold for a fee? Sam Dean assesses the options for player and club in this piece. Out of sight, out of mind could well be the most likely outcome for a player who has missed almost two years of football, and looked extremely raw before his ban.

Looks like a back four once again for Alonso, and Danny Welbeck makes his first Chelsea appearance. Pedro will play off Welbeck as a second striker. Geovany Quenda was signed last year from Sporting CP, but joined up with Chelsea this summer. Another wide forward in their collection.

Chelsea XI: Sanchez; Palestra, Fofana, Tosin, Hato; Caicedo, Nicoll-Jazuli; Quenda, Joao Pedro, Gittens; Welbeck

Chelsea subs: Penders, Sharman-Lowe, Curd, Slonina, Acheampong, Subuloye, Sarr, Diakite, Anselmino, Lavia, Essugo, Watson, Walsh, Kellyman, Mudryk, Estevao Willian, Kavuma-McQueen, Neto, Satpayev, Jackson, Delap

The wheels of commerce continue to turn for Chelsea in the transfer market but this afternoon Xabi Alonso’s team continue their preparations for the new season against Juventus in Hong Kong.

They have the chance to recover from the ignominy of losing to 10-man Tottenham Hotspur in Sydney on Saturday, but with 19 days until Chelsea’s Premier League opener against Fulham these matches are still a fitness building exercise. The positive from the Spurs game was Wesley Fofana, Levi Colwill, Cole Palmer completing 80 minutes – three players who endured injury problems last season.

Another new arrival is expected to follow Morgan Rogers, Marco Palesta, Maxence Lacroix, Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck to Stamford Bridge, with the club nearing a deal for Rayo Vallecano left-back Pep Chavarria.

It wouldn’t be Chelsea without talk of some eye-catching outgoings, with Spurs reportedly interested in Nicolas Jackson and Enzo Maresca eyeing a reunion with Pedro Neto at Manchester City.

Alonso’s team promise to be flexible in their tactical approach this season, but so far he has set up with a back four rather than the 3-4-2-1 system he used to such great effect at Bayer Leverkusen. That could change as availability increases closer to the start of the season, but Palestra’s bursts forward from right-back in tandem with Estevao have caught the eye.

Juventus finished sixth in Serie A last season under Luciano Spalletti, the former Roma and Napoli coach who usually guarantees expansive and attractive football. Turkey left-winger Kenan Yildiz was their top goalscorer last season, and it looks like they will make it through the summer without the left-winger being picked off by one of the Premier League’s elite. Yildiz scored 11 goals in all competitions, and Dusan Vlahovic was the only other player to reach double figures so scoring goals is a problem to address. Lois Openda and Randal Kolo Muani have been signed this summer to strengthen the forward line.

#1696. Chelsea news: Estevao Willian provides fresh comments on playing time frustration after latest Brazil appearance

By Darren Plant | 17 Nov 2026 20:14

Chelsea winger Estevao Willian has thanked Brazil manager Carlo Ancelotti for his "trust" during the international break.

The 19-year-old's lack of starts for Chelsea since the arrival of Xabi Alonso has been a regular topic of conversation.

Although the Spaniard placed more faith in the playmaker prior to the November international break, Estevao was still dropped after an encouraging performance versus Manchester United on October 31.

However, Ancelotti has recently insisted that Estevao's game time for Chelsea will not negatively impact on his role for the national team.

That stance has since been proven through the former Palmeiras starlet featuring for 128 minutes across friendlies versus Japan and Singapore.

During Tuesday's 7-0 win over Singapore, Estevao contributed one goal and two assists before his 70th-minute withdrawal.

Speaking to ESPN after the game, Estevao admitted that he was grateful for the support that he had received from Ancelotti.

He said: "I'm very happy to have gotten minutes in the friendlies.

"I thank Ancelotti for his confidence, because every player wants to play and at Chelsea I've had few minutes, but coming here and knowing that the manager trusts me gives me a lot of motivation."

With Kallang - the venue for Tuesday's friendly - eight hours in front of England, Estevao is essentially getting extra rest ahead of Saturday's Premier League game versus Leeds United.

Nevertheless, not only will it take his body clock time to reset, the likes of Cole Palmer, Danny Welbeck and Emanuel Emegha - players competing for roles in the final third - have not represented their countries during the international break.

Meanwhile, Morgan Rogers was back in the country on Monday after representing England, so Estevao is essentially at a disadvantage when it comes to trying to dislodge teammates from the starting lineup.

All things considered, it is highly likely that he will take a place on the substitutes' bench.

#1695. Opinion: Andoni Iraola forced to sacrifice 95-goal Liverpool star to sign €70m midfielder

Andoni Iraola has tried his best to turn Liverpool's fortunes around at Anfield since his arrival.

Last term, the club were performing well below expectations and ended up finishing fifth in the Premier League.

In a normal season, managing to qualify for the Champions League would be seen as a decent outcome but, after spending £450 million on new players and winning the title just a season before, it was a bad performance.

Their lack of form resulted in Arne Slot being sacked and left Iraola to deal with all of his shortcomings.

Most of the time, things have gone well but, for them to get even better, changes are going to have to take place in the upcoming transfer window.

Liverpool would have to sell Dominik Szoboszlai or Ryan Gravenberch to sign Lamine Camara

Liverpool's midfield has been one of their main problems since 2023.

The July of 2023 was when Fabinho exited Anfield and, since then, the Reds haven't had a natural number six among their ranks.

Alexis Mac Allister, Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch have all been used there to try and plug the gap.

And, while Gravenberch did fairly well during the Reds' title-winning season, from that point on, he's failed to meet expectations.

That's why in the 2026-27 summer transfer window, fans were sure that a new number six would be brought in.

Obviously, Richard Hughes and Iraola didn't feel the need to do that, even though the Spaniard's double pivot has been the thing to cause them the most issues so far.

Several different players were linked as potential options for the Reds to explore but, according to an update from David Lynch via Anfield Index, the Reds would have to sell Gravenberch or Szoboszlai to make room for someone such as Lamine Camara.

"I know the reports, but still struggle to see Lamine Camara to Liverpool in January without a significant departure," he said.

"Endo doesn’t play at all, more a Gravenberch or Szoboszlai which it’s hard to see, otherwise there’s a questions of minutes. Liverpool don’t like to be over stocked as we know."

Liverpool would have to spend around €70m to sign Lamine Camara

Before the 2026-27 season got fully underway, Liverpool were heavily linked with Camara.

In fact, some outlets were even reporting that a deal for the Senegal international was going to be done before the end of the transfer window.

That obviously never ended up happening and now, they're being linked once again with the form of Szoboszlai and Gravenberch raising a fair few questions.

But, for the Reds to sign Camara, it's been reported that a fee worth around €70 million would have to be spent for AS Monaco to even think about letting him go.

Since they rejected his move to Chelsea during the dying embers of the window, he's gone from strength to strength and now, the Ligue 1 outfit are seeing that he's worth a lot of money.

Right now, nothing is decided but, sacrificing someone such as Szoboszlai feels like a big leap, especially for an unproven player in the Premier League.

By Ben Knapton | 17 Nov 2026 20:21, Last updated: 17 Nov 2026 20:21

Tottenham Hotspur have been urged to make an approach for AC Milan midfielder Youssouf Fofana, who could be one of the "top five" players in his position in the Premier League.

The Lilywhites spent big to reinforce their engine room during the summer with the signings of Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes for a combined £185m, while Rodrigo Bentancur, Lucas Bergvall and Conor Gallagher remain on the books too.

However, a report from Italian outlet Calciomercato states that Tottenham are 'ready to attack' for Fofana, who is currently on loan at Sevilla from Milan and has made a positive impression in La Liga.

Fofana has scored one goal and provided three assists in nine Spanish top-flight appearances, but he is only under contract with Milan until 2028, and his long-term future remains unclear.

Speaking exclusively to Sports Mole, former Milan striker Mark Hateley implored Tottenham to make a move for Fofana, whom he believes everyone would be casting their eye on if he became available.

"That's the type of player all top clubs would look for, even as a bit-part player," Hateley said. "He's one of those players who'll get into the side and be good in it, and then out of the side if need be.

“There are a lot better players out there, but he is a good player. That's the difference between the top three, four, five clubs now. You can pay £50m or £60m for a guy who's just going to be knocking around the squad, and that's where we are in the football world right now.

“He'd be one of the top three, four or five in England anyway; we'd all be looking at that sort of player if he became available.

“Spurs are still struggling to find something at the moment. It's normally the player you never imagine is going to make everybody else work: the squad player, your £30m or £40m, maybe £50m player, and it works.

“That's where we are with Tottenham right now. I've seen them play very well this season, but I've also seen them play very, very poorly, and that's the frustration with supporters, because you don't know which team is going to turn up. It's not an 11 you're building right now, it's an 18 or 19-man starting line-up."

Reportedly valued at just £12.5m by AC Milan, Fofana does not trump his Spurs rivals in many statistical columns, but the 27-year-old is superior to Fernandes, Tonali, Gallagher and Bentancur on a few metrics.

Fofana's 0.38 assists per 90 minutes is the highest total among the quintet, as is his 1.15 successful dribbles per game, from 3.56 attempts; Gallagher is second in the latter statistic with 1.42.

Fofana has also been dispossessed on the fewest occasions - just 0.76 times per 90 minutes - and was no stranger to a direct involvement during his first two seasons with Milan.

The ex-Monaco man has scored three goals and set up 13 more in 88 games for the Rossoneri, although he was left out of France's World Cup squad and has not represented Les Bleus since 2024.

Mark Hateley was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of London.Bet.

#1691. Deal complete: Chelsea owners steal in before Liverpool's FSG

Chelsea's owners, Blue Co., have swooped in to steal a deal ahead of Liverpool and FSG. This wasn't how things were supposed to go.

Everything changed at Liverpool in early 2024 as Jurgen Klopp got ready to leave the club. The German's exit provided an opportunity for an overhaul - and a move towards a new plan.

Liverpool's owners FSG welcomed back Michael Edwards and Julian Ward, installing Richard Hughes as sporting director. Edwards and Ward, however, weren't strictly working for Liverpool but instead headed up a new multi-club project.

Multi-club projects, while correctly controversial, are an increasingly common occurrence in football as elite clubs look to consolidate their position. FSG wanted a piece of that and instructed Edwards to help lead the search for more clubs to bring under their ownership.

The idea, however, fell flat. FSG consistently failed to find a club for a reasonable price and eventually cancelled the plan around two and half years after kicking it off.

Blue Co. sign Vitor MatosSwansea City coach Vitor Matos has, per Fabrizio Romano, agreed to take over at Strasbourg. The French side are owned by Chelsea's owners Blue Co. and they'll now take the highly-rated coach under their wing. Swansea have been enjoying life under Matos and it's no surprise that he's been given a 'bigger' gig. However, this was supposed to be FSG making the move.

Swansea City coach Vitor Matos has, per Fabrizio Romano, agreed to take over at Strasbourg. The French side are owned by Chelsea's owners Blue Co. and they'll now take the highly-rated coach under their wing.

Swansea have been enjoying life under Matos and it's no surprise that he's been given a 'bigger' gig. However, this was supposed to be FSG making the move.

Matos, after all, was one of Klopp's assistants at Liverpool and only left the Reds when the German did. He embarked on a career as a head coach but Sunday Times correspondent Jonathan Northcroft claims the plan was always to bring him 'back'.

'Back' meaning to a club under the FSG flag, in other words. Matos was viewed as one for the future and someone who could help lead the development at a different club. You'd imagine the potential for him to rejoin Liverpool as head coach was there, too.

Instead, it's the Chelsea group who've got him. Matos is heading there with Strasbourg and it feels as though the Reds have missed their chance.

#1690. Wayne Rooney opens up on mental health struggles, drinking and seeking help from a therapist

By Alexis Pereira | 17 Nov 2026 20:39

Wayne Rooney has revealed that he contemplated suicide during his time at Manchester United. The former England captain, 41, spoke about it on the Life at the Midpoint podcast, hosted by Gabby Logan, describing a period when his eldest son Kai was still a baby. The interview was reported by the BBC and also picked up by Sky Sports.

‘I got to a place where you’re contemplating suicide,’ Rooney said. ‘You just didn’t want to be around anyone. I didn’t want to see people in the streets. I didn’t want to go into shops.’

Rooney was speaking about years when he was at his best on the pitch. According to the BBC, Kai is now 17, so the period was roughly 17 years ago. He describes it as a time when he had just got married and just had a son.

‘It should be the happiest point in my life, and it wasn’t,’ he said. Asked by Logan about the hardest moment of his life, he said that when he was drinking he would shut himself at home for two days and just drink, at what was probably the best phase of his career in playing terms.

He joined United from Everton in 2004 and, according to the BBC, became the club’s all-time top scorer with 253 goals in 559 games. He won five Premier League titles, the Champions League, the Europa League, the FA Cup and three League Cups before returning to Everton in 2017. He remains a legend at Old Trafford, where Mauricio Pochettino is now beginning his time as boss.

‘I was always comfortable on a football pitch, but everything else, I really struggled with it,’ he said on the podcast.

Rooney also explained why nothing showed on the outside at the time. ‘You don’t want to show any weakness, so you try to mask it,’ he said. He said a feeling that he would be less of a man stopped him admitting his own state. In the end he confided in his wife Coleen and his mother and started speaking to a therapist. He now describes his behaviour at the time as selfish. ‘Coleen helped me enormously,’ he added. ‘She could have left, it was that bad, but she stayed by me and helped me get through it.’

This is not the first time Rooney has spoken about a dark period. In February 2022, when the Rooney documentary came out on Amazon Prime Video and he was managing Derby County, he told the PA news agency, as reported by The42, that he suffered inside for a long part of his career and that a lot of it ended in drinking. He also told the Mail on Sunday, as reported by Inside World Football, that in his early years at United, until about the birth of Kai, he would shut himself at home and drink. He pointed to the pressure of playing for England and United and what the newspapers wrote about his private life. According to PA, he saw a psychologist only briefly at the time.

The new interview is a significant step on from those earlier accounts. In the 2022 pieces, the subjects were alcohol and the pressure of fame, with no mention of suicidal thoughts. Rooney did, however, explain then why he stayed silent as a player. He said he could not go to older players such as Roy Keane or Ryan Giggs and say there was a problem. He added that today it is much easier, because mental health is talked about and problems are caught earlier, especially among young players.

England’s most famous striker of his generation could not speak about his state while he was playing, and speaks most openly about it as a former player and television pundit. He has been named pundit of the year at the Broadcast Sport Awards and currently appears in the ITV reality show I’m a Celebrity. The subject has remained relevant in dressing rooms, as goalkeeper James Trafford showed recently when he left Manchester City over his mental health.

If you or someone you know is struggling, support is available. In the UK, Samaritans can be called free at any time on 116 123.

Published: 18:10 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 19:58 EST, 15 November 2026

Thomas Tuchel hailed the 'best performance of my time as manager' after England beat world champions Spain in a crazy, brilliant see-sawing drama of a Nations League tie.

England played the best football of Tuchel's two-year reign as coach to end Spain's world record 43-match unbeaten run.

But they played the last half an hour of the game with ten men after Elliot Anderson was sent off for pulling back Lamine Yamal.

Spain got two goals back to set up a nerve-wracking finish but goalkeeper James Trafford, in the team ahead of Jordan Pickford, pulled off a miracle double save in the dying minutes to seal the win.

'What a performance we put out there for 60 minutes to be deservedly 3-0 up,' Tuchel said after the game. 'Thirty minutes against Spain with ten men feels like three hours.

Thomas Tuchel said England's display in the win over Spain was the best in his time as boss

'It is the best performance of my time and they are unbeaten for 43 matches and that was a complete performance in that environment. To impose our identity on them was a real achievement.

'Declan Rice said he knew we were going to win and I could feel the true belief. This was the moment we wanted to prove ourselves. You need to rely on your teammates. That is why I am very proud of the win.'

Tuchel also questioned the decision to give Anderson a straight red, made by a referee he once labelled a 'one out of 10'.

The Man City midfielder was sent off because Clement Turpin adjudged him not to have been making an attempt to play the ball when he fouled Yamal.

'The red card and the penalty is always a big decision and I needed to understand why it was a double punishment but... OK,' Tuchel told ITV Sport.

#1687. Arsenal lock down defence as Hincapie joins Rice and Raya in contract talks

By Alexis Pereira | 17 Nov 2026 20:53

Arsenal are in advanced talks with Piero Hincapie over a new contract, according to the BBC, despite the defender having more than four years left on his current deal. The Ecuador international, 24, is the third key player to be tied down in a single week after Declan Rice and David Raya. BBC football correspondent Sami Mokbel says he is set to sign a 12-month extension on improved terms even if he is strongly linked to Barcelona in the last weeks.

On Monday evening, Sky Sports News reported that Rice, 27, had verbally agreed a new deal with Arsenal. On Tuesday morning, Sky Sports, citing The Athletic, reported in its live coverage that goalkeeper Raya, 31, had also agreed a new long-term contract. His current deal runs to 2028, and the Spaniard has won the last three Premier League Golden Gloves, according to Sky. The report came shortly after Raya admitted he would one day like to play in La Liga.

Arsenal have not officially announced any of the agreements, but the BBC says the club are preparing to confirm new contracts for Rice, Raya and Jurrien Timber. Riccardo Calafiori, 24, is also next in line, according to the BBC. The Italian left-back, who joined from Bologna in 2024, has a contract until the summer of 2029, and the club want to begin talks with him in the not-too-distant future.

Hincapie joined on 1 September 2025 from Bayer Leverkusen on a season-long loan with an option. The BBC reported at the time that Arsenal had agreed a £45m fee for a permanent deal, and saw the Ecuadorian as a direct replacement for Jakub Kiwior, who left on loan for Porto. Boss Mikel Arteta introduced him on the club website, saying: ‘Piero is physically really impressive, and his versatility and tactical flexibility give us strong options in defence.’

On 25 June 2026, the club announced they had exercised the option and the move became permanent from 1 July, without disclosing the fee. According to Arsenal, Hincapie made 39 appearances in all competitions in the title-winning season, was the club’s player of the month in February and April, and scored his only goal in February at Wolverhampton Wanderers. The defence he slotted into conceded the fewest Premier League goals for the third season running, according to the club.

The BBC now gives 47 appearances for Arsenal in total, which suggests he has added eight this season. One of them was the November game in Prague, where Arsenal beat Slavia Prague 2-1.

The Hincapie deal is not a protection against losing him for free, as that risk does not exist with more than four years remaining. A one-year extension on better terms looks mostly a reward and a way of aligning his wages with the role he has in the squad. He has gone within a year from a loan replacement for Kiwior to a player the BBC lists among the key members of Arteta’s squad.

The common thread in all three cases is timing. Rice had 18 months plus an option left, according to Sky, Raya had a deal to 2028 and Hincapie more than four years. Arsenal are not negotiating under pressure from expiring contracts, which sends a clear signal that, after the title, they want to build on the existing core. In Raya’s case there is also a defensive logic, as the goalkeeper himself opened the subject of Spain and a new contract makes such temptations more expensive. If Timber is added, and Calafiori in the coming months, Arteta will have a goalkeeper, three defenders and the driving force of midfield all on new contracts.
